common_name: Picasso African Violet (Fantasy-Patterned Large Variegated Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks. Picasso, registered in 1988, is a long-established large-growing fantasy-pattern cultivar still popular on the show table.

directions: Grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix, allowing the surface to dry slightly between thorough waterings. Picasso is a large-growing fantasy cultivar with double light-blue-and-white flowers whose splashy markings vary from bloom to bloom, set off by variegated foliage that shows white speckling at the leaf margins and a pink blush on new growth at the crown. Because both the flower fantasy pattern and leaf variegation are unstable, expect some variation between cuttings and select the most strongly marked leaves for propagation. Give this cultivar extra space and a larger pot than a typical standard, since it is bred to reach an unusually full, exhibition-scale rosette.
